sourceFacts: One circuit diagram has two filled junction dots, a on the left and b on the right, with an incoming external wire at a and outgoing external wire at b.

The upper physical path rises from a, turns right, enters the left face of the upper hollow rectangle, exits its right face, continues right and descends into b. Its resistor is R1, labelled beneath its rectangle.

The lower physical path descends from a, turns right, enters the left face of the lower hollow rectangle, exits its right face, continues right and rises into b. Its resistor is R2, labelled above its rectangle.
These are exactly two physical a-to-b branches. Neither resistor has an interior bypass wire or an external bypass.
An I arrow above the incoming left lead points right toward a. I1 above the upper resistor points right, and I2 below the lower resistor points right.

Between the two branches, a horizontal V comparison has opposing left and right heads indicating the a/b span. V is labelled above it. It is not a conducting center branch and must not be counted as a short circuit.

The complete instructional label set is a, b, R1, R2, I, I1, I2 and V. Node labels lie below/beside their own dots. There are no numeric values, source, meter, switch, additional resistor or second panel.

At the upper-left image boundary there is a clipped isolated black fragment and a small mark, disconnected from all circuit geometry and without a legible instructional label. They are scan-edge residue, not source apparatus to reproduce.
